extraction.name: XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations
extraction.description: XTREME-S is a benchmark to evaluate universal cross-lingual speech representations in many languages. It covers four task families: speech recognition, classification, speech-to-text translation and retrieval, spanning 102 languages from 10+ language families, 3 different domains and 4 task families.
extraction.creator: Alexis Conneau, Ankur Bapna, Yu Zhang, Min Ma, Patrick von Platen, Anton Lozhkov, Colin Cherry, Ye Jia, Clara Rivera, Mihir Kale, Daan Van Esch, Vera Axelrod, Simran Khanuja, Jonathan H. Clark, Orhan Firat, Michael Auli, Sebastian Ruder, Jason Riesa, Melvin Johnson
extraction.publisher: Google Research, Hugging Face, Meta AI
extraction.citeAs: Conneau, A., Bapna, A., Zhang, Y., Ma, M., von Platen, P., Lozhkov, A., Cherry, C., Jia, Y., Rivera, C., Kale, M., Van Esch, D., Axelrod, V., Khanuja, S., Clark, J. H., Firat, O., Auli, M., Ruder, S., Riesa, J., & Johnson, M. (2022). XTREME-S: Evaluating Cross-lingual Speech Representations. arXiv:2203.10752v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark uses existing datasets: Fleurs (speech version of FLoRes), MLS (Multilingual LibriSpeech), VoxPopuli, CoVoST-2, Minds-14. Fleurs was newly collected: 2009 n-way parallel sentences from FLoRes dev and devtest sets in 102 languages, with 1-3 recordings per sentence (2.3 average), and new train-dev-test splits (1509, 150, 350 sentences).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Direct measurement, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Fleurs is complete at more than 97%; some slight improvements and changes may be done in a 2nd version (e.g., missing recordings, replaced low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Fleurs uses sentences from FLoRes machine translation benchmark. MLS derived from read audiobooks of Librivox. VoxPopuli from European Parliament sessions. CoVoST-2 from Common Voice and other sources. Minds-14 from e-banking domain.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For Fleurs, new train-dev-test splits were built with 1509, 150, and 350 sentences for train, dev, and test respectively. For MLS, the official 10-hour splits were used. For VoxPopuli, languages with more than 10 hours of data were selected. For Minds-14, monolingual datasets were merged into a single multilingual dataset with a 30-20-50% train-dev-test split.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Fleurs: recordings collected for each sentence. CoVoST-2: translations from 21 languages into English. Minds-14: intent labels from e-banking domain. Fleurs-LangID: language labels derived from the language of the sentence.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Datasets and fine-tuning scripts are made easily accessible through the HuggingFace platform. Fleurs may have a 2nd version with updates (missing or low-quality recordings).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Making speech technology available in all languages is important to give speakers of under-represented languages an equal voice on the Internet.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Results are much better on Western European languages (11.5 average WER) than on Sub-Saharan African (26.7) or South Asian (20.7), partly due to larger amounts of unlabeled data in WE languages.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Tasks are focused on linguistic aspects of speech; nonlinguistic/paralinguistic aspects are not evaluated. Test sets are not hidden, so users must avoid overfitting.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The benchmark is designed to evaluate multilingual speech representation learning.
